route: A fold fed back into its own drive: can the affine cascade carry the counter, or is every feedback fold a cascade
object: THE FEEDBACK FOLD (def:ff): a fold cascade F_0,...,F_D whose normalised differences obey psi_d = mu_d eps_{d-1} psi_{d-1} - 1 (one player) or psi_d = mu_d (eps_{d-1}psi_{d-1})_+ - 1 (two players) with gains mu_d >= 2 and psi_0 = 2t-1, in which the drive t is not a frozen payoff but the value of a vertex whose first-passage row is supported by the cascade's own vertices, so that the strategy determines the drive (as the fixed point of a monotone contraction of loop gain lambda_sigma < 1) and the drive determines the switchable set; the all-switches dynamics is then an explicit map on the pair (cube point, drive).
headline: Every all-switches step of a fold cascade -- one player or two, drive frozen or fed back -- is one of only m maps B_i indexed by the level i at which the strategy first disagrees with the drive's itinerary, and the mismatch level strictly increases unless the drive leaves its dyadic cell.

results.name: The B-map: every all-switches step of a fold is one of m maps
results.statement: Let a fold cascade of m = D+1 levels have gains mu_d >= 2 and be nondegenerate at sigma, with sign vector eps and drive t_sigma, and let i be the least level at which eps disagrees with the itinerary gamma(t_sigma) of the greedy orbit psi^gr_d = mu_d|psi^gr_{d-1}|-1, psi^gr_0 = 2t-1 (i = infinity if there is none). If i = infinity no F_d is strictly switchable. Otherwise the sign vector of sigma[S_sigma] is B(eps,i) with B(eps,i)_d = eps_d for d < i, B(eps,i)_i = -eps_i, and B(eps,i)_d = -prod_{k=i+1}^{d-1} eps_k for d > i; and S_sigma = {d : eps_d != B(eps,i)_d}, min S_sigma = i. Hence from any sigma the all-switches step has at most m possible outcomes, indexed by i alone, whatever the drive is and whether or not it is fed back; the same formula holds with an average partner (one player) and with a Min partner (two players).
results.why_not_implied: rem:one-player-fold proves only that under a FIXED strategy the OF(D) cascade is affine and that OF(D), being acyclic, halts within D+1 rounds by thm:component-bound; it neither identifies the all-switches map nor covers a cascade carrying a cycle (a fed-back drive) or a Min partner, and the suffix parity rule -prod eps_k appears nowhere in the paper.
results.argument: F_d is strictly switchable iff eps_d != sign(psi_d), so the new sign vector is d -> sign(psi_d). For d <= i all lower signs match, so both recursions reduce to psi_d = mu_d|psi_{d-1}|-1 and sign(psi_d) = gamma_d. Above i, eps_i psi_i < 0 forces psi_{i+1} <= -1 (one player) resp. psi_{i+1} = -1 (two players), so |psi_{i+1}| >= 1 and sign(psi_{i+1}) = -1 = the empty product. Inductively, if |psi_d| >= 1 with d > i then |mu_{d+1} eps_d psi_d| >= 2 > 1, so sign(psi_{d+1}) = sign(eps_d psi_d) = eps_d sign(psi_d) and |psi_{d+1}| >= mu-1 >= 1 (two players: psi_{d+1} is either mu|psi_d|-1 or exactly -1). Writing n_d = sign(psi_d), n_{i+1} = -1 and n_{d+1} = eps_d n_d, which is the display. Full proof in result.tex and NOTES.md section 2.
results.verification: Checked round by round FROM THE GAMES: on FF1(D), D = 1..8 (one-player feedback folds, n = 7D+6), 410 rounds at D = 8 and every round of every start for D <= 5; on FF2(D), D = 1..6 (two players, n = 6D+6), 280 rounds at D = 6. At each round the switched set computed from val_sigma (min over ALL Min strategies) was compared with B(eps, min S) and the drive t = val_sigma(u) was checked to lie in J(eps,i): no failure anywhere. Scripts games.py, run.py; games in FF_games.json.

results.name: The mismatch level climbs unless the drive leaves its cell
results.statement: Along an all-switches run of a feedback fold the drive t_k = val_{sigma_k}(u) is nondecreasing (lem:switch), and if t_{k+1} lies in the same cell J_k = J(eps_k,i_k) as t_k then i_{k+1} > i_k, where J(eps,i) = {t : gamma_d(t) = eps_d for d < i, gamma_i(t) = -eps_i} is an interval (for a tent fold, the dyadic interval of length 2^{-(i+1)} carrying that prefix). Consequently the run splits into at most E+1 segments of length at most m, E being the number of rounds at which the drive leaves its cell, so L <= m(E+1); a fold with a constant drive has L <= m; and a run of length L forces the drive to cross monotonically at least L/m - 1 cell endpoints -- for a tent fold, points of the dyadic grid 2^{-m}Z. In particular a superpolynomially long fold run requires the drive itself to be a monotone counter through that grid.
results.why_not_implied: thm:component-bound bounds an all-switches run by sum_j (2^{|C_j|}-1) over the strongly connected components of the Max-reachability digraph, which for a feedback fold is a single component of size m and gives 2^m - 1; it says nothing about the order in which levels fire, and cannot yield the bound m for a constant drive on a cyclic game nor the conversion of a long run into a monotone dyadic sweep.
results.argument: sigma_{k+1} has sign vector B(eps_k,i_k), which by the B-map theorem agrees with gamma(t_k) on {0,...,i_k}. If t_{k+1} is in J_k then gamma(t_{k+1}) agrees with gamma(t_k) there, so eps_{k+1} agrees with gamma(t_{k+1}) on {0,...,i_k} and the first mismatch is above i_k. Within a segment i_k < i_{k+1} < ... are distinct levels, so a segment has at most m rounds; and t is monotone so each cell endpoint is crossed at most once. J(eps,i) is an interval because along the greedy orbit psi^gr_d is affine in t while the signs are prescribed.
results.verification: The monotonicity of the drive and the interval membership were read off the games in exact arithmetic: for FF1(1), FF1(2), FF2(1), FF2(2) the full lists of drives along every run are recorded (e.g. FF1(2) from start (X,Y,Y): t = 39/232, 11/60, 47/248, strictly increasing, mismatch levels 0 then 1); over all runs of FF1(D), FF2(D), D <= 6, the containment t_k in J(eps_k,i_k) held at every one of the 410 + 280 rounds checked. Independently, exhaustive search over the B-map graph shows the combinatorial ceiling is NOT the obstruction: with cells and a monotone drive the longest B-map path is 2^m - 1 (measured 1,3,7,15 at m = 1,2,3,4, mono.py).

results.name: Level zero of a feedback fold fires at most twice
results.statement: At most two rounds of an all-switches run of a feedback fold have mismatch level 0; equivalently the bottom Max vertex F_0, whose two options are the drive and a constant, switches at most twice.
results.why_not_implied: cor:selfread characterises when a self-reading Max vertex is strictly switchable and computes what its switch gains; it does not bound how often it switches, and the bound here is obtained from the monotonicity of the drive along the run together with the B-map (eps_0 can change only at a round of mismatch level 0), not from the excursion identity.
results.argument: eps_0 changes only at rounds with i_k = 0, and at such a round it is set to gamma_0(t_k) = sign(t_k - q_0). Since t_k is nondecreasing, once that sign is +1 it stays +1 and no further level-0 mismatch can occur; so at most one round sets eps_0 to -1 and at most one later round sets it to +1.
results.verification: Observed on every run of FF1(D), FF2(D), D <= 6, and it is exactly tight on the first blow-up level's walk, whose mismatch sequence is 0,0,2,1 (blowup_test.py, b1lp.py).

results.name: The drive response of a feedback fold
results.statement: For strategies sigma, sigma' of a feedback fold, t_{sigma'} - t_sigma = (sum_v w_v delta_v)/(1 - lambda_{sigma'}), where delta_v = val_{sigma'}(v;t_sigma) - val_sigma(v;t_sigma) is the value change at FROZEN drive, w is the drive's first-passage row and lambda_{sigma'} = sum_v w_v A_v^{sigma'} is the loop gain; consequently t_{sigma'} - t_sigma <= max_{v : w_v > 0} delta_v/(1 - A_v^{sigma'}), with 1 - A_v the probability that the token from v reaches a sink without visiting the drive.
results.why_not_implied: thm:impedance writes the gain of a switch inside ONE fixed game as a transfer impedance over an escape probability; the present identity is about the FIXED POINT of a feedback loop -- it separates the frozen-drive gain from the loop gain and bounds the drive's move by a maximum, over the readable vertices, of (frozen-drive gain)/(escape from the drive), a ratio thm:impedance does not form.
results.argument: Phi(t,sigma) = sum_v w_v val_sigma(v;t) + w_1 is affine in t of slope lambda_sigma < 1 with fixed point t_sigma, so t' - t = Phi(t',sigma') - Phi(t,sigma) = lambda_{sigma'}(t'-t) + sum_v w_v delta_v, which is the identity. For the bound, with M the right-hand side, sum_v w_v delta_v <= M sum_v w_v (1 - A_v^{sigma'}) <= M(1 - sum_v w_v A_v^{sigma'}) since sum_v w_v <= 1.
results.verification: The identity is the defining equation of the drive in every LP built by realise.build_lp / build_lp2 and was used as the exact model of the drive in the exhaustive search; the drive values it predicts agree with val_sigma(u) computed from the games (e.g. FF1(2): 1/7, 47/248, 47/248 along the run from the all-X start), and the bound was the special case that settles m = 2 by hand (NOTES.md section 5).

results.name: At m <= 4 the feedback buys nothing: the longest realisable feedback-fold run is m
results.statement: For a tent fold cascade of m <= 4 levels in the pure form val(X_d) = c_d val(F_{d-1}) + a_d, val(Y_d) = c_d val(Z_{d-1}) + b_d, the longest all-switches run realisable by ANY substochastic average-vertex drive read off the cascade's own values is exactly m, attained only by the mismatch sequence 0,1,...,m-1 -- the run of a constant drive; whereas the B-map alone admits monotone-drive paths of length 2^m - 1. Realisability of a prescribed B-map path is decided exactly by one linear programme in the drive row, and the test is complete because by lem:excursion the drive's value is exactly a substochastic first-passage row over the cascade's vertices and t_1.
results.why_not_implied: prop:one-player-fold and its remark treat OF(D) with a FROZEN drive: the game is acyclic, so all-switches halts within D+1 rounds by thm:component-bound. The present statement quantifies over ALL fed-back drives, for which the Max vertices form a single strongly connected component of the Max-reachability digraph and thm:component-bound permits 2^m - 1; and it is a completeness statement about the drive (an LP characterisation), which the paper has nowhere.
results.argument: By the B-map theorem a run is a simple path of the B-map graph and by the cell corollary its drives are nondecreasing and lie in the intervals J(eps_k,i_k); by lem:excursion the drive's value is a substochastic first-passage row w over the cascade's vertices and t_1, and under a fixed sigma every cascade value is affine in the frozen drive, val_sigma(v;t) = A_v t + B_v, so t_sigma = (w_1 + sum w_v B_v)/(1 - sum w_v A_v) with the denominator positive. Hence the constraint t_sigma in [lo,hi] is the pair of LINEAR inequalities lo(1 - sum w_v A_v) <= w_1 + sum w_v B_v <= hi(1 - sum w_v A_v) in w, and realisability of a prescribed path is exactly the feasibility of the resulting exact LP together with w >= 0, sum w <= 1. A depth-first search over all B-map paths, pruned by that LP (with no constraint imposed on the not-yet-extended last state), is therefore exhaustive; it returns m at m = 1,2,3,4.
results.verification: Exact rational LP (lp.py, two-phase simplex, Bland) inside an exhaustive depth-first search over all B-map paths (search.py, search2.py, searchdy.py). Longest realisable run = 1,2,3,4 at m = 1,2,3,4 for (i) the extremal one-player fold c_d = 1-e_d, e_d = e_{d-1}/(4+e_{d-1}) (e = 1/2,1/9,1/37,1/149, total transmission 0.857), (ii) the extremal two-player fold e_d = e_{d-1}/(2+e_{d-1}) (e = 1/2,1/5,1/11,1/23, transmission 0.673), (iii) the dyadic folds c_d = 1/2 that the games realise. Robustness with the gain-general interval routine gen_J (gains mu_d in {2,3,4}, c_d a random multiple of 1/64 subject to e_d <= 1-c_d): 60 parameter draws at m = 3 and 15 at m = 4, one player and two players -- worst = m in all 150 runs. The m = 5 search was cut short. Cross-checked against the games: FF1(D), FF2(D), D <= 8, maximal run m-1 from every start.

results.name: A fold reads the sign of a difference of its own values, at one Max vertex
results.statement: Let A,B be vertices of a stopping SSG with val(B) < 1 and |val(A) - val(B)| > eta whenever val(A) != val(B), let F -> (A,B) be a Max vertex, let L_0 -> (B,L_1), ..., L_{r-1} -> (B,t_1) be average vertices with eta = 2^{-r}, so val(L_0) = (1-eta)val(B) + eta, and let W -> (F,L_0) be a Max vertex. Then at every profile at which F is optimal, val(F) - val(L_0) = (val(A)-val(B))_+ - eta(1 - val(B)), so W's unique optimal action is F if val(A) > val(B) and L_0 if val(A) <= val(B): the sign of a difference of two of the game's own values is presented to W as a STRICT value comparison, at the cost of one new Max vertex and r = a+1 average vertices (lem:denominator-sharp). Applied to A = X_d, B = Y_d, F = F_d of a fold cascade, W reads sign(phi_d).
results.why_not_implied: rem:blowup-realise records the NEGATIVE fact that no vertex has the anti-value val(j^0)+val(j^1)-val(j), being strictly decreasing in val(j); it does not say that the sign is nevertheless available as a strict comparison between two vertices, nor price it. lem:max-tree binarises an argmax with logarithmic lag; it does not read a sign, and cor:gate concerns zero-tie gating.
results.argument: The chain gives val(L_0) = (1-eta)val(B) + eta by induction (val(L_j) = (val(B) + val(L_{j+1}))/2, val(L_r) = 1). At a profile where F is optimal, val(F) = max(val A, val B), so val(F) - val(L_0) = max(a,b) - (1-eta)b - eta = (a-b)_+ - eta(1-b). If a > b this is a - b - eta(1-b) >= a - b - eta > 0 by the hypothesis on eta; if a <= b it is -eta(1-b) < 0 since b < 1. Both inequalities are strict, so W's optimal action is unique and equals sign(a-b). The bound eta = 2^{-a-1} suffices because every value of a stopping SSG has denominator dividing an integer at most 2^a (lem:denominator-sharp), so a nonzero difference exceeds 2^{-2a}; taking r = 2a+1 is safe and r = a+1 suffices when the two values share a denominator, as they do inside a fold. The gadget reads the sign only once F is itself optimal -- one round of lag, as in lem:max-tree.
results.verification: Built as games and verified from the games: 1024/1024 exact instances with val(A), val(B) every pair of multiples of 2^{-5} realised by dyadic chains and eta = 2^{-6}, checked against w* computed by brute force over all Max strategies (sign.py, games of 15-18 vertices). Embedded in the feedback folds FF1(D), D = 2,3,4, at every level d, with W -> (F_d, L_0) and eta = 2^{-(4D+12)}: in every profile at which F_d is optimal (8, 16, 32 profiles per instance, 12 instances, games of 42-64 vertices) W's strict preference equalled sign(x_d - y_d) -- 100% (signfold.py). The one-round lag is real: in profiles where F_d itself is not yet optimal the read fails, exactly as for lem:max-tree.

results.name: The blow-up escapes the fold model at level two
results.statement: (a) The bottom-antipodal walk 4,3,5,1,0 of B(1-cube) (thm:blowup; the 3-cube orientation (0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2), height 4) is a B-map path in the sense of the B-map theorem under exactly 2 of the 48 relabellings of the cube, with mismatch levels 0,0,2,1; yet the realisability programme is infeasible for it, for the extremal one-player fold, the extremal two-player fold and the dyadic one-player fold alike. So the first blow-up level is combinatorially the walk of a fold, and no drive delivers it. (b) The bottom-antipodal walk 12,19,13,17,8,16,0,7,1,5,4 of B^2 (prop:b2-realised, height 10, m = 5) is a B-map path under NONE of the 3840 relabellings: from level two on the height-doubling device is not a feedback fold at all, and the barrier above does not touch it.
results.why_not_implied: prop:b2-realised exhibits a 138-vertex stopping SSG whose improvement orientation is B^2 and prints its walk; it says nothing about whether that walk is the walk of a cascade of the fold shape, and the B-map class of walks does not exist in the paper. thm:blowup likewise describes the orientation, not the shape of the rule that could produce its walk.
results.argument: Exhaustive over all m! * 2^m relabellings (permutation of the coordinates and complementation of each), testing at each step whether the switched set S satisfies B(sigma, min S) = sigma'. For (a) the two surviving relabellings give the mismatch sequence 0,0,2,1, which is then fed to the realisability LP of the exhaustive theorem, infeasible in all three parameterisations.
results.verification: blowup_test.py (48 and 3840 relabellings, exact bit arithmetic; the blow-up of the 1-cube rebuilt from thm:blowup's rule, sink 0, walk of length 4 confirmed) and b1lp.py (the three LPs, all reported infeasible by the exact two-phase simplex).

restatements.label: rem:one-player-fold
restatements.note: Part (A) asked for the identity 'under a fixed strategy the cascade is affine, psi_d = 2 eps_{d-1} psi_{d-1} - 1'; that sentence is already in the paper, and only its two-player rectifier form psi_d = mu(eps psi)_+ - 1 and the consequences drawn from it here are new.

restatements.label: cor:parity-unreadable
restatements.note: What a fold presents to a downstream Max vertex is a comparison of two substochastic affine functionals -- a halfspace test -- so cor:parity-unreadable already says it cannot read the parity of the inner bottom-antipodal height; the only new content on that point is the price, one Max vertex per read (the sign proposition), so the parity conclusion is recorded as an application, not a result.

restatements.label: thm:component-bound
restatements.note: For a fold with a constant drive the bound L <= m is the component bound applied to the acyclic cascade; the new content of the cell corollary is the same bound for the CYCLIC (fed-back) game, where the component bound only gives 2^m - 1.

gap: The general barrier is not proved. The exact missing sentence: "For every feedback fold of m levels whose drive is a substochastic average readout of the cascade's own values, the all-switches run has length at most m." It is proved here only for m <= 4, by an exhaustive linear programme, and measured at m = 3,4 over 150 further parameterisations. Two smaller gaps: the m = 5 exhaustive search was cut short for time; and the model assumes the drive is an AVERAGE readout -- a drive containing controlled vertices adds cube coordinates and is outside both the theorem and the LP (the B-map theorem itself is unaffected, since it uses only the difference recursion with gains mu_d >= 2).
next_steps: 1. Prove the missing sentence. The shape of the argument that is missing: by the drive-response lemma the drive's move at a round whose switched set lies at levels >= d is at most max_v delta_v/(1-A_v) with every delta_v of order e_d, while flipping level d needs the drive to move by |psi_d| e_0 mu^{-d}; a bound on max_v delta_v/(1-A_v) in terms of e_d that survives loop gains lambda -> 1 would close it. The obstruction is exactly that 1/(1-lambda) is unbounded (thm:impedance), and the LP solutions do exploit it (they put weight 63/64 on the drive's own successor). 2. Run the m = 5 exhaustive LP (search.py 5). 3. Enlarge the model: two coupled cascades, one driving the other's drive; the B-map theorem holds per cascade, so the dynamics becomes a product of B-maps and the question is whether the product escapes the cell corollary. 4. Characterise the B-map walks: since B^2's walk is not one and B(1-cube)'s is, "fold walks" is a new nontrivial subclass of bottom-antipodal walks whose Hamiltonian members (length 2^m - 1, exhibited at m <= 4) are exactly the targets a realisation search should aim at -- and the LP is a complete realisability test for them once the cascade is fixed. 5. Ask whether the one-Max-vertex sign read gives a cheaper route to prop:b3-outer's missing half than the escape shape of def:escape-ext.

prior_art: From memory, flagged unchecked against the sources. The tent-map cascade and its symbolic dynamics are the standard full shift on two symbols (Milnor-Thurston kneading theory); the "itinerary determines the dyadic cell" statement is the classical conjugacy of the tent map with the shift. The drive-response identity is the resolvent/renewal formula (I-lambda)^{-1} for an absorbing chain, i.e. Kemeny-Snell's Green function, and its ratio form is the policy-improvement identity of Markov decision processes (Howard), already named in rem:impedance. The reflected binary (Gray) code order of the tent itineraries is classical. Nothing in the route imports a fifth fact: thm:determinacy, Holt-Klee, Legendre and Samelson-Thrall-Wesler are the only imports, and only thm:determinacy and (through the citation of cor:parity-unreadable) Holt-Klee are used.
